title: Ivo and the Rivergate
premise: Casper Amberdale, a railroad engineer dismissed for refusing to falsify a bridge inspection, takes a contract to survey the closed Rivergate lines before the concession permits expire at first snow. When an exceptional tide exposes a sea cave the locals call the Tollgate, Casper discovers it hides both a shortcut through the range and evidence that his late father's crew vanished there decades ago. Guided by Ivo, a feral boy raised by the last keeper of the gate, and joined by outcasts who become his found family, Casper races the snows while a rival surveyor sabotages the route to steal the permit. At the climax, Casper must choose between sealing the cave to save his companions or holding it open to clear his father's name, and he chooses the people, forging a new identity not as an Amberdale but as the Rivergate's keeper alongside Ivo.
about_author: Edmund Okafor is a former track inspector who spent eleven years mapping abandoned rail corridors across coastal mountain ranges before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people who find belonging in places the maps gave up on.

chapters.title: The Last Inspection
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Refusing to sign off on a rotten trestle costs Casper his job and his reputation in one morning. The emotional beat is quiet humiliation sharpening into resolve as he pockets his father's old map of closed lines and decides to take the only contract left: the Rivergate survey.

chapters.title: A Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In a rented room, Casper studies his father's hand-annotated map, finding a gap where the Rivergate gorge should be. The beat is grief mixed with curiosity; the map ends mid-line, as if his father stopped believing in it.

chapters.title: The Concession Clerk
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A brittle clerk grants him ninety-day permits and warns that renewal is impossible: after first snow, the corridor reverts to the rival Harrow Line. Casper feels the clock start ticking in his chest.

chapters.title: Tide Tables
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with a letter from his mother. Arriving at the fishing village of Greywater, Casper learns locals avoid the shore caves entirely. An old woman tells him the tide will run lowest in three days — 'low enough to show what wants showing.' Foreboding builds.

chapters.title: What the Tide Reveals
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At extreme low tide, a cavern mouth opens beneath the cliffs, its walls carved with rail-gauge notches. Against every instinct, Casper steps inside and finds a rusted lantern stamped with his father's initials. Wonder curdles into dread.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Lives in the Gate
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Inside the cave, Casper is ambushed by a snare and then by Ivo, a twelve-year-old who speaks in rail signals and claims the cave as territory. The beat is mutual suspicion — two survivors measuring each other.

chapters.title: Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo shows Casper the keeper's station deep in the cave: ledgers, tools, and a cot, maintained by Ivo since 'the last keeper stopped coming back.' Casper realizes the last keeper was his father. The beat is stunned inheritance.

chapters.title: The Shortcut Nobody Owns
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The cave passage bypasses forty miles of collapsed line — if Casper can chart it, he finishes the survey before the snows. But using it means trusting a child and a legend. Hope arrives wearing caution.

chapters.title: Harrow Men in Greywater
chapters.summary: Village innkeeper Marta's POV. Surveyor Aldous Vane and his Harrow Line crew arrive asking pointed questions about Amberdale's permits. Marta lies badly and worries worse. The beat is the noose tightening around Casper without his knowledge.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Wrecking Crew
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper hires two rejects: Brigid, a dynamite expert blacklisted for a union speech, and Sefu, a bridge carpenter with a bad leg and perfect memory. Three strangers eat together and, without saying it, begin becoming a crew.

chapters.title: First Passage
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo leads the crew through the cave's upper galleries, testing them with deliberate wrong turns. Casper passes by admitting what he doesn't know. The beat is trust earned through honesty, not competence.

chapters.title: The Gauge That Doesn't Match
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Deep in the passage, Casper finds rails of a gauge used by no company on record — his father's secret experimental line. Ambition kindles: this could be discovery, not just survival.

chapters.title: Vane Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Vane corners Casper in Greywater, offering to buy his permits and bury the cave findings under Harrow's charter. Casper refuses. Vane smiles like a man who expected exactly that answer. Dread settles in.

chapters.title: Sabotage at the Portal
chapters.summary: Brigid's POV. Someone collapses the cave's seaward entrance with charges cut to Brigid's own signature pattern. Trapped inland, the crew must find another way out before the tide cycle floods the lower galleries. Panic becomes discipline.

chapters.title: The Drowned Gallery
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Racing the flood, the crew wades the drowned gallery, Ivo navigating by echo. Sefu's bad leg nearly kills him; Casper carries him the last hundred yards. The beat is the moment strangers stop being strangers.

chapters.title: Out Through the Mountain's Teeth
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. They emerge onto the high plateau via a vent shaft Ivo has never dared use. Below, autumn is already dying. First snow is weeks early. The clock they feared becomes the clock they live by.

chapters.title: Camp of the Unwanted
chapters.summary: Brigid's POV. On the plateau, the crew camps among ruins of a laborers' shantytown. Around the fire, each tells why the industry discarded them. Found family crystallizes — chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Ivo's Name
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Pressed by Brigid, Ivo admits he has no surname — the keeper called him 'the river's boy.' Casper offers his own name and Ivo refuses it gently: 'I'm not an Amberdale. I'm the Gate.' Identity asserted, not given.

chapters.title: The Collapsed Viaduct
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The route hits the viaduct his father's crew died building. Casper finds inspection notes proving the collapse was caused by Harrow's cheap steel, covered up ever since. Rage replaces grief; vindication has a price tag.

chapters.title: Vane on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane's crew shadows them, ordered to let the mountain do the killing. Vane justifies it as business, but a junior surveyor's doubts prick him. The antagonist gains a conscience he'll have to silence later.

chapters.title: Bridge Over Nothing
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. To cross the gorge, Sefu designs a rope-and-timber span from viaduct wreckage. Building it takes four days they don't have. The beat is craft as defiance — making something true in a landscape built on lies.

chapters.title: Crossing
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The crossing goes wrong when a cable frays; Ivo saves Brigid but drops the survey instruments into the gorge. Half their legal evidence is gone. Despair, then Casper's realization: the cave itself is the evidence.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. First flakes fall. Ivo knows winter routes the others don't, but they lead through ground Ivo has never entered — the deep gate, where the last keeper's final entries end mid-sentence. Fear of a place becomes fear of a truth.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Reading by lamplight, Casper deciphers his father's final ledger page: the keeper discovered Harrow's sabotage, planned to testify, and wrote 'if I do not return, the gate must stay open.' His father didn't vanish. He was silenced.

chapters.title: What Ivo Saw
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Flashback chapter: young Ivo watched men in Harrow coats seal the keeper inside the lower gallery years ago and never told anyone, ashamed of surviving. Confession to Casper breaks something open in both of them.

chapters.title: Marta's Telegram
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. In Greywater, Marta risks everything to wire the provincial engineer's office about Vane's sabotage, using Casper's original permit numbers. Small courage, enormous consequence. The outside world begins moving toward the mountain.

chapters.title: The White Silence
chapters.summary: Brigid's POV. A storm pins the crew in a snow cave for three days, food running out. Brigid keeps them alive with routine and stories. The beat is endurance as love — survival measured in shared warmth rather than miles.

chapters.title: Permits Expire
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. By Casper's count, the concession lapsed yesterday. Legally, the survey is worthless; morally, it matters more than ever. Casper chooses truth over paperwork and pushes for the deep gate. Liberation through letting go.

chapters.title: Vane Catches Up
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane's crew overtakes them at the deep gate entrance, weapons drawn, ordering everyone sealed inside 'for safety.' Vane's junior surveyor refuses the order. The confrontation fractures Vane's crew from within.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Deep Gate
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Armed stalemate in the dark. Casper reads the keeper's ledger aloud — the sabotage, the cover-up, the names. Vane's own men lower their rifles one by one. Truth as disarmament; the climax begins.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Avalanche tremors threaten to collapse the gate forever. Blasting it open might kill them all; leaving it shut buries his father's proof. Casper hands the detonator decision to Ivo — the Gate's true keeper. Trust at the point of no return.

chapters.title: Ivo Decides
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo sets the charge to open the gate, saying 'the river doesn't keep things. It carries them.' The blast roars; the passage holds, barely. Catharsis — the boy who survived by hiding chooses openness.

chapters.title: Descent of the Engineer's Office
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Government inspectors, summoned by Marta's telegram, arrive through the opened gate to find a standoff resolved, a living witness (Ivo), and physical proof of Harrow's steel. Vane is taken down the mountain in custody.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In Greywater's overheated hall, Casper testifies; so does Vane's junior surveyor. Casper declines to restore his old name or job, asking instead that the Rivergate corridor be chartered honestly. Justice without revenge.

chapters.title: Charter of the Gate
chapters.summary: Brigid's POV. The province grants a new charter: the Rivergate line, built to the experimental gauge, with the cave preserved as a working passage. Brigid, Sefu, and Casper are hired to build it. Vindication shared four ways.

chapters.title: Naming Rights
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the registry, officials ask the boy's full name for the keeper's appointment. Ivo writes 'Ivo of the Rivergate' — a name he made himself. The theme lands: identity is authored, not assigned.

chapters.title: First Rail
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Spring comes; the crew lays the first rail of the new line through the gate. Casper drives the spike his father never got to drive. Grief transmuted into foundation — literally and emotionally.

chapters.title: The Train Comes Through
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The first train enters the cave, whistle echoing through galleries Ivo once guarded alone. Ivo stands at the keeper's post, lamp lit, waving it through. Belonging achieved; solitude ended.

chapters.title: Low Tide Again
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A year later, at extreme low tide, Casper walks the shore where it began and leaves flowers at the cave mouth for his father. The wilderness forgave nothing, but people did. Quiet gratitude.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger, Continued
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, closing frame. Ivo opens a fresh ledger page and writes the first entry in his own hand: names of the crew, the date, the words 'gate open.' The story ends where keeping begins — family recorded, future entrusted.
